reconstruction_rules.rule: Declaration order can determine DS versus ES code generation: the compiler keeps the last-loaded far selector live, so the order in which far objects are first referenced in the source (not the extern declaration order) fixes ES reuse and the CONST selector-pool order. Reorder references, not declarations, to change selector traffic.

When the historical code holds a parameter's value in SI/DI throughout, an explicit local copy of the parameter (register variable candidate) can be required; the compiler does not enregister [bp+n] parameters directly.

Arrays are frequently word-indexed (SHL 1 / ADD reg,reg before the displacement). Preserve the observed element width: declare int arrays for two-byte strides, char arrays for byte strides, eight-byte structs for SHL 3.

Never invent a convenient symbol when MAPSYM provides the real one: use the exact name from direct_data_bindings; an unnamed operand inside a named public array is an index into that array, not a new private object.

A matching numeric offset does not establish object identity: equal offsets in different segments are different objects, and a BSS word placed by constraint inside another object's data proves nothing.

Far-object identity requires selector/segment evidence: an NE selector relocation on the slot or immediate that loads ES, resolved to the object's segment. Prefer the packet's addressed_segment and exact_mapsym_names.

Reconstruct private state as natural static data with an evidence-backed size, type and initializer (a static in _DATA when the original bytes are initialised, in _BSS only when the original word lies in the BSS region), never as address-padding arrays.

The CONST selector pool is private to one object and ordered by first reference across the whole unit; a function whose pool constraints conflict in isolation needs its unit context, and functions sharing a pool word belong to the same unit.

The compiler profile belongs to the unit context (layout/compiler-profiles.json): use the packet profile as given; a code-shape mismatch that only /Og explains is profile evidence for the unit (report it), not a per-function flag to try.

Dx8 (segment 8 offset 0) and Dy8 (offset 8) are two MAPSYM symbols; in objects whose pool block holds two adjacent segment-8 words for them (simtwo:3EF8 C57E/C580, simant:6A38 BF70/BF72) index each with the bare direction (`Dx8[i]`, `Dy8[i]`), never `Dy8[i+8]` or `(Dx8+8)`; one word per symbol. The one-Dx8-object spelling applies only where a single word serves all displacements.

Values computed only to feed a call are emitted in argument push order (right to left), not statement order: when the target loads `Dy8` before `Dx8` the call is `f(..., lx, ly)` with ly the last argument. Reorder arguments/locals before rewriting expressions.
YMapPopB (seg 8 +0xA4) and YMapPopR (+0x164) are 12x16 byte maps indexed `(x << 4) + y`, each through its own selector word; the symbol supplies the base displacement (do not add 0xA4/0x164).

struct OpenDB (PACK _openDBData, 0x7C-byte slots): name[0x50]; void far *indexTable @0x50; int recordCount @0x54; pad to 0x6C; int count @0x6C; long freeBytes @0x6E; long wastedBytes @0x72; int pad @0x76 (never referenced); int file @0x78; int dirty @0x7A. Deleted/replaced record lengths are added to wastedBytes.

Never reach a PACK word as `match_position[K]`: the object allocates one selector word per symbol, so the public at PACK offset 2K (`ListIndexB`, `TemBModePop[i]`, `FlyAwayR`, ...) must be named; `tools/rebind_pack_index.py` rewrites and re-verifies such sources. Isolated admissions with this spelling are byte-exact but bind the wrong word in the unit.
